item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is preferable because it avoids B’s visible compatibility change and tests replay using a genuinely non-seekable source, but neither patch satisfies the frozen contract and neither should merge unchanged.","reasons":["A leaves the existing WithFilesRequestOptions API untouched; B changes its declared return type from FilesOption to FilesRequestOption, contrary to the requirement that FilesOption behavior remain unchanged and potentially breaking callers that use the function as a typed value.","A’s Upload retry test uses io.MultiReader, directly verifying that buffered streamed content can be replayed. B’s retry test uses strings.Reader, which is already inherently replayable and therefore provides weaker coverage of the reported scenario.","A’s seekable-body tests also cover preservation of a nonzero starting offset and explicitly verify non-replayable bodies are not retried, making its additional retry work better characterized.","Both candidates introduce prohibited association-option machinery, use the wrong Upload option type, bypass FilesService.Add, extend the multipart helper instead of directly reusing NewFile, and modify unrelated Raw.Do retry behavior. A wins only on relative merge quality."],"risks_a":["Upload has opts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required opts ...FilesOption.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request, decoding, and error logic.","It adds association fields and multiple WithUpload* APIs explicitly excluded by the contract, plus a new multipart NewForm abstraction not requested by the task and additional README/changelog claims around them lying outside scope discipline relative to the frozen contract requirements for exactly the convenience API behavior specified (even though documenting changes is generally good practice). Additionally, the wording 'exactly this convenience API' is violated by the extra public association option surface, not merely by documentation itself. It also modifies Raw.Do replay and ownership semantics despite the instruction not to refactor retry machinery and to preserve Add behavior. The Upload tests omit source-reader failure coverage required by the contract."],"risks_b":["Upload has opts ...FilesUploadOption instead of the required opts ...FilesOption.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating established Add behavior.","It adds seven prohibited association options, extra ID validation semantics, FilesRequestOption, multipart Field, and NewFileWithFields machinery, substantially expanding scope beyond the requested convenience wrapper and violating the contract's prohibition on association fields and duplicate machinery. It changes the exported return type of WithFilesRequestOptions, creating a visible compatibility risk despite interface embedding. It modifies Raw.Do and therefore Add/Update replay and reader-closing behavior, explicitly outside the allowed scope. Its retry test uses strings.Reader rather than a non-replayable streamed source, and it provides no source-reader error test."]}
